Incumbents typical work assignments may include the following: -Develops and applies substantive knowledge and experience in DoD and OSD programs and activities; OSD Acquisition and Sustainment missions, policies, and objectives; management principles and processes. - Employs analytical and evaluative methods and techniques for assessing program development or execution to independently, as well as in collaboration with NC3 stakeholders, analyze the complex NC3 capability portfolio and its system of systems to ensure it is fully responsive to all essential performance, compatibility, and interoperability requirements, is cost-effective and not duplicative. Applies results to promote effective and efficient evolution of the portfolio. - Coordinates and collaborates with appropriate NC3 stakeholders to balance requirements, funding, acquisition strategies, and program execution necessary to deliver capability to warfighters and enable National Defense Strategy objectives in accordance with DoD budgetary and financial management principles and techniques. - Conducts analysis, develops strategies and roadmaps, and presents results to USD(A&S), Joint Staff, and OSD forums that oversee NC3 capability portfolio modernization. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-9 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability in: 1) Applying writing and editing techniques and correspondence regulations and procedures in order to prepare a wide variety of written materials; OR 2) Reviewing and ensuring appropriate coordination of draft responses utilizing automated correspondence management tools; OR 3) Managing the requirements for handling executive level correspondence. OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M., if related from an accredited college or university. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Combination of Experience and Education: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ARE YOU APPLYING FOR A PROMOTION? If you are a current or former Federal Civilian employee and applying for a higher grade than the grade that you currently or formerly held within the last 52 weeks, it is recommended you provide SF-50(s) that show you have held the next lower grade for at least one year. Some SF-50s effective within the last 52 weeks will not demonstrate you have held the next lower grade for at least one year (e.g. General Adjustment SF-50 from this year). A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Classified Support Branch (CSB) of the Correspondence Management Division (CMD); Executive Services Directorate (ESD), Washington Headquarters Services (WHS). CMD is responsible for providing administrative support and executive staff assistance to the Secretary of Defense (SecDef), Deputy Secretary of Defense (DepSec), the Executive Secretary (ExecSec) of the Department of Defense, and their immediate senior staffs.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) is a world-class service organization, with a dynamic workforce and unwavering commitment to service excellence. WHS is the essential services provider for the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Department of Defense (DoD) agencies, and offices in the National Capital Region.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as duty officer on a rotating shift basis in the CSB. Establishes procedures for controlling, tasking action assignments, dispatching, and filing of a wide variety of classified correspondence addressed to or emanating from the SecDef, DepSec, and the DoD ExecSec. Reviews classified correspondence to ensure that it is marked with proper security classification to include: classification markings, declassifications statements, and special security caveats at page, subject, and paragraph to ensure that markings are in accordance with DoD Manual 5200.01 "DoD Information Security Program." Follows established procedures for controlling and tasking on NIPR and SIPR Correspondence and Task Management System (CATMS) action assignments of a wide variety of classified correspondence. Analyzes the incoming correspondence for action agency, type of action required, suspense date by which action must be completed, required coordinators, information agencies, and ensures appropriate signatory level for replies are accurate and complete.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as an Executive Officer for the Deputy Chief of Staff G-8, Executive Services Division, located at the Pentagon, Arlington, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.

Coordinate responses and suspense's as it pertains to official DoD and HQDA taskings, personnel actions, executive level-SES/GO briefings/presentations.

ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. All qualifications and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Office of Force Resiliency (OFR) in the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (OUSD(P&R)). The Executive Director, Force Resiliency, serves as the principal advisor for policy to the USD(P&R) and DUSD(P&R) for all matters related to Force Resiliency. Primary responsibilities include serving as advisor for legislative and public affairs issues and analyzing potential impact of Congressional initiatives on current policies.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as a subject matter expert and advisor on developing and implementing strategic communication plans, outreach and engagement, stigma reduction initiatives, and partnership-building initiatives. Develops and coordinates implementation and evaluation of a strategic communication plan for the Office of Force Resiliency (OFR) and develops strategic communication messaging and partnership-building aspects of resiliency activities. Identifies opportunities for continued development, implementation, and refinement of force resiliency strategic communication and outreach program efforts of the Department and Military Services. Assists in the promulgation of resiliency information and resources for all members of the Armed Forces and their families to ensure availability from their initial enlistment/appointment through their final retirement or separation. Monitors legislative initiatives, active legislation, congressional correspondence, hearings, congressional visits, briefings, and internal and external communications concerning the OFR; monitors Congressional Engagements with Legislative Affairs (LA), OSD. Monitors Congressional floor actions, bills, and amendments through the House, Senate, and Conference sessions until signed into law by the President; attends and/or monitors hearings to ensure consistency of policy statements among DOD leadership.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GG/GS-13 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector performing duties such as: Analyzing historic analytic efforts to identify and recommend the most impactful analytic pillar(s) that will help to close critical capability gaps. Coordinating with the Analytic Master Plan (AMP) pillar leads to conduct tailored research in support of emerging information warfare (IW) concepts and future information warfare (IW) capabilities. Serving as the lead action officer to provide N2N6 Divisions with analytically rigorous capability gap assessments and quantitative analysis in support of Program Objective Memorandum (POM) decisions. Representing N2N6 as subject matter expert on USN and Joint working level integrated process teams and working groups. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Management Analyst at the GG-14 grade level in the Integration Branch of the Information Warfare Future Capabilities Division to provide analytic support for N2N6 and utilizes extensive knowledge of Information Warfare to lead analytic pillar(s) within the Warfighting Integration Division (OPNAV N2N6I) Analytic Plan.
Details.SubAgencyName: DCNO for Information Warfare, Warfighting Integration, IW Future Capabilities
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will coordinate with military, government civilian, and contractor personnel to develop and execute capability studies, assessments, and comparative analysis products of existing and future information warfare capabilities.
You will utilize knowledge of information warfare to lead analytic process within the Division.
You will provide all IW Divisions with integrated analysis to support Program Objective Memorandum (POM) investment decisions.
You will represent the Division as subject matter expert to working level integrated process teams and working groups.
You will identify information gaps in information warfare focused areas and recommend analysis processes to eliminate these gaps.

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability in: 1) managing a parking program and operating its IT system software/application to ensure parking assignments are determined for various parking requirements; 2) developing parking plans and conducting survey reports; and 3) operating a Mass Transportation Benefits Program related to subsidized parking to de-conflict/determine parking requirements. OR Education: Ph.D degree or equivalent OR 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree OR a PH.D. or or equivalent doctoral degree, if related. OR Combination of Experience and Education: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) is a world-class service organization, with a dynamic workforce and unwavering commitment to service excellence. WHS is the essential services provider for the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Department of Defense (DoD) agencies, and offices in the National Capital Region.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as advisor to the Director and Parking Manager on Pentagon Reservation parking issues. Assists with administering the operation of the Pentagon Reservation Parking Program, to include commercial and government agency parking. Performs studies and surveys to determine requirements and levels of use for different types of parking. Assists with the development and implementation of a system that matches parking database names with those of mass transit applicants for all subsidized parking facilities in the National Capital Region (NCR). For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the length of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/
You may qualify at the GS-12 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your experience with an enterprise scalable system used for creating, delegating, assigning, responding and researching a knowledge repository linked with task and correspondence accurately and efficiently on a Non-Secure and Secure Internet Network and managing the administrative lifecycle of an organizational-wide audit or investigation for high level management from the initial intake, maintaining liaison with high level management, to completing various tasks and corrective action plan implementation. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Details.JobSummary: The incumbent serves as a highly motivated self-starter who works independently and with senior executives at the Office of Secretary of Defense (OSD) or Component levels.as an Executive Assistant for the Executive Director, Force Resiliency (EDFR), Office of Force Resiliency (OFR), OUSD(P&R) supporting OFR and its programs. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as the Executive Secretary for the Office of Force Resiliency (OFR) performing a range of direct executive office support for the Executive Director, Force Resilience (EDFR) and OFR's front office staff; serves as the point of contact for coordination, development, and interpretation of policies and coordinates the flow of information among program activities. Provides all executive administrative support functions for the front office; provides direction, advice, and assistance to management and employees on administrative issues and for the automated systems supporting correspondence for the office. Reviews all correspondence/packages for content, accuracy, and completeness; serves as the correspondence control representative and primary point of administrative contact and liaison with external offices and individuals on operational and programmatic matters. Oversees and tracks tasks and requests from the Government Accountability Office (GAO), DoD Inspector General (IG), and Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) for OFR programs and provides guidance for timely and quality submissions. Completes special projects as directed and provides formal and informal, written and oral briefings to senior staff members on various issues and projects, and performs action officer duties in support of OFR functions and requirements.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the length of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/ You may qualify at the NH-4 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the NH-3 (GS-13) grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your experience in supporting military construction, facility investment, and construction programs with specific experience in sustainable features associated with the design and construction of facilities. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. Details.JobSummary: Responsible for overseeing the DoD's military construction and facilities management programs to provide U.S. forces with installation assets and services in a cost effective, safe, sustainable, and environmentally sound manner.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition & Sustainment (OUSD(A&S)) (ODASD(CON))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Supports the development and collection of data on DoD facility and infrastructure requirements and resources, to include foreign government (Host Nation) cash funded and in-kind construction. Performs in-depth analyses on DoD facility and infrastructure requirements and resources including Host Nation cost sharing/funding to determine their propriety and effectiveness. Organizes and directs the review and analysis of a variety of complex problems, issues, studies and plans. Assignments may include but are not limited to: (a) evaluating new or alternative concepts for improving facility acquisitions, facility sustainment, and modernization; (b) designing criteria and techniques to evaluate effectiveness of resource levels; (c) performing oversight of the execution of construction programs such as the Energy Resilience and Conservation Infrastructure Program, European Deterrence Initiative, and Pacific Deterrence Initiative; (c) developing strategy, plans, and policy for cost sharing/funding programs and management tools to analyze funding requirements; and (d) participating on U.S. teams to negotiate cost sharing agreements with Host Nations with respect to DASD(Con) facilities programs. Initiates programs, actions and taskings to ensure adherence to DoD policies and procedures, and ensures that programs accommodate operational requirements and promote the readiness and efficiency of the armed forces. Participates in the various stages of the DoD Planning, Programming, and Budget Execution System for DASD(Con) programs. Develops and initiates management techniques and practices to facilitate the critical review and analysis of DASD(Con) programs.

ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.JobSummary: Responsible for overseeing the DoD's military construction and facilities management programs to provide U.S. forces with installation assets and services in a cost effective, safe, sustainable, and environmentally sound manner.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition & Sustainment (OUSD(A&S)) (ODASD (CON))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Supports the development and collection of data on DoD facility and infrastructure requirements and resources, to include foreign government (Host Nation) cash funded and in-kind construction. Performs in-depth analyses on DoD facility and infrastructure requirements and resources including Host Nation cost sharing/funding to determine their propriety and effectiveness. Organizes and directs the review and analysis of a variety of complex problems, issues, studies and plans. Assignments may include but are not limited to: (a) evaluating new or alternative concepts for improving facility acquisitions, facility sustainment, and modernization; (b) designing criteria and techniques to evaluate effectiveness of resource levels; (c) performing oversight of the execution of construction programs such as the Energy Resilience and Conservation Infrastructure Program, European Deterrence Initiative, and Pacific Deterrence Initiative; (c) developing strategy, plans, and policy for cost sharing/funding programs and management tools to analyze funding requirements; and (d) participating on U.S. teams to negotiate cost sharing agreements with Host Nations with respect to DASD(Con) facilities programs. Initiates programs, actions and taskings to ensure adherence to DoD policies and procedures, and ensures that programs accommodate operational requirements and promote the readiness and efficiency of the armed forces. Participates in the various stages of the DoD Planning, Programming, and Budget Execution System for DASD(Con) programs. Develops and initiates management techniques and practices to facilitate the critical review and analysis of DASD(Con) programs.

Develop written organizational policies, procedures and SOPs.

Evaluate organizational programs, identifies errors, tracks and monitors operations, tasks, and completions of numerous HR programs and projects, recommending/implementing change to programs/projects across traditional civilian HR functional lines.
Address management and workforce training, manpower, payroll and budget, EEO, employee and management relations, and administrativepolicies; applies extensive knowledge and tact in these areas.
Prepare reports and briefings, reports, management reviews, training classes.

Manage automated civilian personnel information, management, and communication systems sufficient to develop, initiate, and execute actions in support of civilian personnel management, organizational.
Analyze facts, identify problems, report findings, make conclusions, and recommend corrective or other appropriate action.
Identify and develop payroll data, retrieve information from payroll systems, analyze payroll variances, and generate standard reports for seniorleadership.
Analyze organization civilian personnel requirements, determines administrative needs, and takes action to ensure requirements are met.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the length of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/ You may qualify at the NH-04 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the NH-03 (GS-13) grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your experience in maintaining and implementing directives, instructions, and other guidance related to Special Access Programs policy and administration. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; and, Beginning and ending dates of appointment. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.JobSummary: Serves as the senior Policy and Governance advisor to the Director, Deputy Director, and staff of the Directorate of Special Programs. The Director of Policy and Governance is responsible for maintaining and implementing DoD Directives, Instructions, and other guidance documents related to SAP policy and administration. Leads SAP Central Office task management/coordination process, and the Corporate Portfolio Program Initiative for the Defense Industrial Base and the DoD.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition & Sustainment(OUSD(A&S))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties:
Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: - Serves, on behalf of the Director of DoD SAPCO, as the primary interface with DoD Components, Federal Agencies, Industry, and others for matters related to DoD Special Access Program (SAP) oversight and governance policy
- Develops, monitors, and updates SAP oversight and governance policy in collaboration with key SAP stakeholders
- Directs, develops, and manages processes for providing oversight of DoD SAPs
- Plans, coordinates, and facilitates execution of DoD SAP governance forums
- Initiates actions to resolve SAP oversight and governance issues and implements/promulgates solutions
- Conducts studies, provides risk assessments, & directs support for strategic and/or time-sensitive SAP matters
- Represents DoD on interagency committees and commissions concerning all matters within the scope of assigned responsibilities
- Analyze new or proposed legislation or regulations to determine impact on SAP oversight and governance policy
- Provides DoD views on SAP language and legislation to Congressional Defense Committee Members and Professional Staff
- Assists with preparation of the SAP Annual Report to Congress and other required reporting requirements
- Develops implementation policy consistent with Title 10 Section 119 USC, E.O. 12958, DoDD 5205.7, DoDI 5205.11, and DoDI S-5230.28. - Establishes long-range processes that contribute to more favorable/predictable outcomes for new and existing SAPs
- Manages the Contractor Portfolio Program

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the five Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs), the Mandatory Technical Qualifications, and other qualifications, if applicable, listed below. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS: All applicants must submit written statements (narrative format) describing accomplishments that would satisfy the ECQs. You must address each ECQ separately, not to exceed 10 pages. You are required to respond to all ECQs. If you fail to do so will result in a rating of 'ineligible.' When responding to the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs), you must clearly show that you possess the experience, knowledge, skills and ability to perform the duties of this position by submitting narrative responses in which you detail your experience in each of the ECQs. Your examples should be clear and emphasize your level of responsibilities, scope and complexity of programs managed, program accomplishments with results of your actions, policy initiatives and level of contacts. You should limit your narrative to two pages per ECQ, and address each ECQ separately. OPM's Guide to Senior Executive Service Qualifications can assist you in writing an effective SES application. In particular, please note the Challenge-Context-Action-Result Model that is recommended and very helpful when drafting ECQ narrative responses. The Guide is available on OPM's Website at:
http://www.opm.gov/ses/references/guidetoSESQuals_2012.pdf Applicants must utilize the Challenge-Context-Action-Result (CCAR) Model when writing Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ). Use two examples of relevant experience for each ECQ being sure your experience matches the ECQ criteria.
Challenge - Describe a specific problem or goal.
Context - Describe the individuals and groups you worked with, and/or the environment in which you worked, to address a particular challenge (e.g., clients, co-workers, members of Congress, shrinking budget, low morale).
Action - Discuss the specific actions you took to address a challenge.
Result - Give specific examples of measures/outcomes that had some impact on the organization. These accomplishments demonstrate the quality and effectiveness of your leadership skills. Each accomplishment should be clear, concise, and emphasize your level of responsibilities; the scope and complexity of the programs, activities, or services you managed; program accomplishments; policy initiatives undertaken; level of contacts; the sensitivity and criticality of the issues you addressed; and the results of your actions. You should use action oriented leadership words to describe your experience and accomplishments (e.g., Led the development and implementation of....) and quantify your experience wherever possible to demonstrate your accomplishments (e.g., number of employees supervised; size of budget managed; amount of money saved, etc.). ECQ 1 - Leading Change: This core qualification involves the ability to bring about strategic change, both within and outside the organization, to meet organizational goals. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to establish an organizational vision and to implement it in a continuously changing environment. ECQ 2 - Leading People: This core qualification involves the ability to lead people toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to provide an inclusive workplace that fosters the development of others, facilitates cooperation and teamwork, and supports constructive resolution of conflicts. ECQ 3 - Results Driven: This core qualification involves the ability to meet organizational goals and customer expectations. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to make decisions that produce high-quality results by applying technical knowledge, analyzing problems, and calculating risks. ECQ 4 - Business Acumen: This core qualification involves the ability to manage human, financial, and information resources strategically. ECQ 5 - Building Coalitions: This core qualification involves the ability to build coalitions internally and with other Federal agencies, State and local governments, nonprofit and private sector organizations, foreign governments, or international organizations to achieve common goals. Applicants that are either Career SES members, or graduates of the Office of Personnel Management Certified Development Program are not required to address the ECQs. MANDATORY TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS: All applicants must submit written statements (narrative format) of accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications. You must address each technical qualification separately. You are required to respond to all of the technical qualifications. If you fail to do so, you will be rated as ineligible. Please limit your written statements to no more than two pages per technical qualification. 1. Must have expert knowledge of the current organization, structure, and functions of the Department of Defense and its major Components; as well as the Executive and Legislative Branches of the Federal Government to include knowledge of the functions and coordinating relationships between U.S. Government Departments and Agencies, and working relationships of and between branches of Government.
2. Demonstrated experience in applying organizational, management, and governance principles and practices in a very large government organization having dynamic programs of national and international significance.
3. Ability to conceptualize large and complex issues and identify innovative approaches to address challenges in the missions areas of DoD, or a large Federal entity or organizational equivalent. DoD Joint Enterprise-Wide Experience Statement: In addition, DoD requires an Enterprise Perspective. This individual must have the ability to apply a broad point of view and an awareness and understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to DoD or government-wide strategic priorities is required. Executives must demonstrate ability to work with internal and external partners to support national security objectives. This perspective is typically gained through a variety of diverse work experiences. A separate narrative statement is not required. This information should be embedded within the application package (Resume, Technical Qualifications and Executive Core Qualifications).

Details.JobSummary: The Director, Organizational and Management Policy (O&MP), is responsible for advising and assisting the Secretary of Defense, Deputy Secretary of Defense, Director, Administration and Management (DA&M), Office of the Secretary of Defense Principal Staff Assistants (PSA), Defense Agencies and Field Activities (DAFA) Directors, and other senior Department of Defense (DoD) officials on organizational and management problems and issues.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Director, Administration and Management
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the Offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, and General Counsel. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES), a small, elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants.
MajorDuties: The Director, O&MP is responsible for managing and directing timely and effective solutions to DoD-wide managerial and organizational problems and for devising improved organizational, functional, and managerial arrangements for the administration of DoD activities and programs. Major duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Providing context, advice, and assistance to inform senior DoD officials on reorganizations, transfers of functions and responsibilities, establishment and disestablishment of DoD organizations and officials, and the authorities and relationships of and between major DoD Components. Serving as mandatory policy reviewer on all DoD issuances and other relevant documents, as required. Managing and codifying responsibilities, functions, and authorities in DoD Chartering Directives and serving as the office of primary responsibility for the development and maintenance of charters for the OSD PSAs; DAFA's; and other major DoD organizations, activities, or officials. Developing near-term agendas and long-term objectives consistent with national/defense security strategies, ensuring read aheads/briefing materials are developed/refined for decision-making by DoD leaders, and recording/synthesizing deliberations. Responsible for oversight, management, and engagement, on behalf of the DA&M, for the full range of issues related to legislative affairs and legislative counsel matters including engagement and coordination with senior leadership and staff within the Offices of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Legislative Affairs, Director of Budget and Appropriations Affairs within the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Comptroller, and the Deputy General Counsel for Legislation within the Office of the General Counsel of DoD. Responsible for support and development of DA&M products for engagement with Congressional Members and Staffers, preparing responses to inquiries from Congress, monitoring and communicating information on appropriations and authorization related activities, providing analytic support and expert advice on legislative issues, and tracking and responding to inquiries and engagements from the Office of Management and Budget and the White House Legislative Affairs Office.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: This position is designated by the Air force as a Test Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Testing Program. As a mandatory requirement for employment in this TDP, the incumbent is (A) to refrain from use if required, to submit to urinalysis testing. The selectee must sign a statement acknowledging the position occupied is identified as a TDP. This is a KEY position IAW AFI 36-507. Duties of this position are essential to the accomplishment of wartime/contingency operations. Incumbent of key positions must be removed from their military recall status if alternative for filling of the position during an emergency are not available. In order to qualify, you must meet specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Management and Program Analysis, GS-0343. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience include: detailed knowledge of: the substantive nature of Operations Directorate programs and activities; agency missions, policies, and objectives; management principles and processes; and the analytical and evaluative methods and techniques for assessing program development or execution; detailed knowledge that supports work on the Command's Strategic Vision and the Commander's highest priority issues; extensive knowledge of the NC/J3 staff procedures used to accomplish special projects and prepare position papers, briefing, and other documentation used by the Directorate to arrive at position on a variety of issues ranging from planning for and executing resources to Congressional issues. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of qualitative and quantitative techniques in analyzing operational warfighting requirement. Knowledge of joint mission, methods, practices, procedures, regulations, policies, and processes to formulate, justify, and integrate directorate/organization goals in support of Homeland Defense, Theater Security Cooperation, and Defense Support of Civil Authorities missions. Knowledge of the DOD planning and programming (PBR, PPBE, JROC, JCTD, NMS, NSS, and NDS) processes in order to participate in operational requirements development. Knowledge of the roles and organizations of the DoD, interagencies, and the Department of Homeland Security. Ability to staff, inter and intra-command operations-related tasking and similar tasking from Joint Staff to develop well- thought, thorough, and accurate responses and positions for the directorate. Knowledge of Joint Staffs strategic vision policies, processes, and procedures to include Joint Capability Areas, Capability Portfolio Management and Functional Capability Board activities. Knowledge of the roles and organizations of the Services, OSD, and the Department of Homeland Security. Ability to staff, inter and intra command operations-related tasking and similar tasking from Joint Staff. Skill in written and oral communications to present sensitive recommendations concerning various issues. Ability to plan, organize, develop projects and to negotiate effectively with management and other groups to accept and implement recommendations, where proposals involve substantial resources and may be in conflict with previous programming decisions. Ability to gather, organize, and analyze resources management independently devising solutions to complex management problems. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
"This is a Supervisory Position." A 1 year supervisory probationary period is required if applicant selected has not previously met this requirement. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions, 0301 Series. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-14, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes knowledge of a broad range of Joint training, exercise, and war gaming programs, knowledge of the application of military planning, and coordination activities within a Combatant Command Headquarters, and with the Joint Staff, OSD, Allied Military Organizations, and U.S. Government Agencies; and Knowledge of missions, strategies, goals, objectives, processes of COCOM and its Components, Regions and Subordinate Headquarters. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-14 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-15 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of a broad range of Joint training, exercise, and wargaming programs
2. Knowledge of the application of military planning, and coordination activities within a Combatant Command Headquarters, and with the Joint Staff, OSD, Allied Military Organizations, and U.S. Government Agencies.
3. Skill in developing and/or integrating specialized software and technologies for enhanced information and knowledge management and for analytical studies.
4. Knowledge of missions, strategies, goals, objectives, processes of NORAD and USNORTHCOM and its Components, Regions and Subordinate Headquarters.
5. Skill in applying military decision making and military planning and coordination processes.
6. Skill in the application of methods and techniques to assess and evaluate program effects. Skill in managing multiple and simultaneous complex projects and programs. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions of subordinates, and appraise the subordinate's performance of duties. Ability to analyze, plan, and adjust work of subordinates to meet requirements and objectives within available resources. Skill in oral and written communication. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Knowledge and skill in applying analytical, evaluative, and investigative methods and techniques to issues concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of group administrative and support program operations. Knowledge of the laws, regulations, policies and precedents which affect group programs and related support resources. Knowledge of training goals and objectives to assist in the management and implementation of training goals for the CSS personnel. Knowledge and understanding of a comprehensive range of staff concepts, objectives, policies, management/organizational techniques, and military command. The primary purpose of this position is to administer and direct the group's executive support functions and to ensure that day-to-day operations comply with the policies of the group commander/Senior Air Reserve Technician (ART) and command.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win...Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. MajorDuties: Serves as the executive advisor on programs and initiatives within the group. Performs a variety of staff studies concerning group programs and program support effectiveness resulting from regulatory changes, new technology, program/mission changes, recurring requirements, and others. Represents the group commander concerning group plans, special events, projects, etc., to communicate the commander's policies and to explain the interests of the group in regard to local activities or projects. Manages group resources for executive support, services and activities. Maintains oversight of and has overall responsibility for the inspection program as it relates to the group and directs the conduct of inspection activities. Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: This is a "Key" position. It cannot be vacated during national emergency or mobilization without seriously impairing the capability of the organization to function effectively. Unless an alternate can be designated to perform the duties of this position during wartime, the incumbent of this "Key" position must be screened from military recall status. This is a Mission Essential (ME) position performing a Mission Critical Function (MCF) which must continue uninterrupted after the occurrence of an emergency and continued through full resumption of all functions. IAW, DoDI 3020-42, Defense Continuity Programs. This position is designated by the Air Force as a Test Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Testing Program. As a mandatory requirement for employment in this TDP, the incumbent is (A) to refrain from use of illegal drugs and (8) if required, to submit to urinalysis testing. The selectee must sign a statement acknowledging the position occupied is identified as a TDP. May be required to perform Battle Roster functions during Exercise and Real World events. Battle Roster functions may include, but are not limited to, Joint Personnel Operation Cell, Contingency Command Center, Future Operations Center, Joint Enabling Capability, and other tasks as assigned. These duties may require additional duty hours and/or alternate duty locations. This position has been identified as eligible for situational telework. The position eligibility is separate and distinct from the employee's eligibility. Telework for civilian employees is a discretionary workplace flexibility, not an entitlement. Employee and their supervisors must complete the DD Form 2946, DoD Telework Agreement, prior to participation in telework programs. Civilian employees who will telework must complete the required training within 30 days of appointment. Under DODI 1035.01_DAFI 36-816, Telework Program, a civilian employee's telework arrangement may be terminated at the discretion of the supervisor or at the employee's request. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions, Series 0343. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes mastery knowledge of DOD authorities, its Civil Support and P&ID missions, and respective programs, including its functions and processes to accomplish DOD Coordinating Authority for Pandemics and Infectious Diseases (P&ID), and coordination with USG agencies; mastery knowledge of Chairman, Joint Chiefs of Staff Joint Strategic Planning System processes; mastery knowledge of DOD strategies, policies and plans including, but not limited to, the Unified Command Plan, Guidance for the Employment of the Force, Contingency Planning Guidance, Joint Strategic Campaign Plan, National Defense Strategy, National Military Strategy, and other National and DOD strategic guidance related to National security and P&ID; and expert knowledge of Emergency Management principles. mission areas. and core functions, and the managerial functions associated with disaster planning and response. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of Joint operational doctrine and the relationships between the various combatant command missions and organizations. 2. Knowledge of Joint Operation Planning and Execution System and traditional Military Decision Making Process, and skill in the application of joint planning expertise as it applies to assigned programs and strategic and long-range planning functions. 3. Knowledge of the DOD, Joint Staff, and Services strategic planning documents and development processes of the Joint Strategic Planning System. 4. Knowledge and understanding of P&ID to include DOD organizations and Federal agency missions, capabilities, organization and operations. 5. Ability to lead a large, highly diverse group of mid to senior level military/employees from a wide spectrum of private, Federal agencies, departments, and various levels of government including state and local agencies. Leadership must be exhibited in an environment of competing agency interests, loyalties, and agendas, and must be exercised with extraordinary diligence and sensitivity, as the incumbent holds no supervisory authority in the traditional sense. In this environment, the incumbent must find a way to get this diverse group to work together effectively and productively to achieve the goals and objectives of interagency coordination and cooperation. 6. Ability to gather, assemble, and analyze facts, draw conclusions, conduct analysis, devise recommended solutions, and package the entire process in briefings, papers, or reports suitable for senior USNORTHCOM leadership use and decision-making. Skill in preparing oral and written communications. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
